$$\mathrm{pH} = -\log[10^{-10}] = 10$$

That means, the $\mathrm{pH}$ value will rise from $7$; the $\mathrm{pH}$ value of the alkaline solution is more than $7$. The significance of $\mathrm{pH}$ value $7$ is that the solution is neither alkali nor acidic; it is a neutral solution. When the value of $\mathrm{pH}$ is less than $7$, the solution is acidic. When the value of $\mathrm{pH}$ is more than $7$, the solution is alkaline.

Measurement of $\mathrm{pH}$ is done using a $\mathrm{pH}$ scale.

**pH Scale:** Although in mathematical terms, the value of $\mathrm{pH}$ may be any number from negative to positive, in reality, the value is measured on a scale of $0$ to $14$.

The $\mathrm{pH}$ of a neutral solution is $7$. You have already seen that the value of acidic solution is less than $7$ and the value of alkaline solution is more than $7$. According to the scale, the strongest acid will have a value of $0$ and the strongest alkali will have the value of $14$.

**Measuring System:** You have already learned how to measure $\mathrm{pH}$ of a solution from the molarity of its hydrogen ion. Now you will learn how to measure it in experiments. The process involves the universal indicator, $\mathrm{pH}$ paper, $\mathrm{pH}$ meter etc.

**Universal Indicator:** Universal indicator is the mixture of various acid and base indicators. Universal indicator turns to different colours for different values of $\mathrm{pH}$. There is a chart of colours for different values in the Universal indicator.
